points.point: Most Districts continued to expand at a modest-or-moderate pace
points.quote: Most of the twelve Federal Reserve Districts reported that their economies expanded at a modest or moderate pace from mid-October through late November, though both Dallas and Philadelphia noted slower growth compared with the prior Beige Book period.
paraphrases: Most Districts kept expanding at a modest or moderate pace.
Economic growth was modest to moderate in most of the twelve Districts.
Overall, the majority of Districts reported modest-to-moderate expansion.
decoys: Most Districts reported sharp contraction in economic activity.
Dallas and Philadelphia both reported slower growth than the prior period.

points.point: Dallas and Philadelphia both reported slower growth than the prior Beige Book period, a divergence from most Districts' steady pace.
points.quote: though both Dallas and Philadelphia noted slower growth compared with the prior Beige Book period
paraphrases: Dallas and Philadelphia both saw growth decelerate versus the previous report.
Growth slowed from the prior period in the Dallas and Philadelphia Districts.
Unlike most Districts, Dallas and Philadelphia noted a deceleration in growth.
decoys: Dallas and Philadelphia both reported faster growth than the prior period.
St. Louis and Kansas City noted slower growth compared with the prior period.

points.point: Labor markets tightened further across a broad range of occupations.
points.quote: Labor markets tightened further across a broad range of occupations.
paraphrases: Labor markets grew even tighter across many occupations.
Job markets tightened further, spanning a wide range of occupations.
Labor market conditions kept tightening broadly across many occupations.
decoys: Labor markets loosened somewhat across a broad range of occupations.
Housing markets tightened further across a broad range of regions.

points.point: More than half of Districts said firms' growth was constrained by an inability to attract and retain qualified workers
patterns: (half|majority) of.{0,20}districts.{0,80}(inability to attract|inability to retain|hiring difficult\w*|difficulty (hiring|finding workers)|constrain\w*).{0,40}(worker|labor|staff|employee|growth|hiring)?|(inability to attract|inability to retain|hiring difficult\w*|difficulty (hiring|finding workers)|constrain\w*).{0,40}(worker|labor|staff|employee|growth|hiring)?.{0,80}(half|majority) of.{0,20}districts
points.quote: Over half of the Districts cited firms for which employment, production, and sometimes capacity expansion had been constrained by an inability to attract and retain qualified workers.
paraphrases: Over half of Districts said hiring difficulties were constraining growth.
More than half the Districts reported firms unable to attract and retain qualified workers, limiting expansion.
A majority of Districts cited an inability to attract and retain workers as a constraint on growth.
decoys: Only a couple of Districts reported any difficulty attracting workers.
Labor markets tightened further across a broad range of occupations.

points.point: Tariff-driven cost increases spread further down the supply chain, from manufacturers and contractors to retailers and restaurants.
points.quote: Reports of tariff-induced cost increases have spread more broadly from manufacturers and contractors to retailers and restaurants.
paraphrases: Tariff-related cost pressures broadened from manufacturers to retailers and restaurants.
Cost increases tied to tariffs spread further, hitting retailers and restaurants in addition to manufacturers.
Tariffs pushed costs higher down the supply chain, now affecting retailers and restaurants too.
decoys: Tariff-induced cost increases receded, easing pressure on manufacturers and retailers.
Reports of energy-induced cost increases have spread more broadly to retailers and restaurants.

points.point: Wage growth broadly tended toward the higher side of a modest-to-moderate pace across Districts.
points.quote: most Districts reported that wage growth tended to the higher side of a modest to moderate pace
paraphrases: Wage gains leaned toward the upper end of the modest-to-moderate range in most Districts.
Most Districts saw wage growth running at the stronger end of modest-to-moderate.
Wage increases tilted toward the faster side of the modest-to-moderate pace nationwide.
decoys: Most Districts reported that wage growth tended to the lower side of a modest to moderate pace.
Most Districts reported that price growth tended to the higher side of a modest to moderate pace.

points.point: Input costs continued to outpace final goods prices, squeezing margins
points.quote: Nearly all reported that input costs rose faster than final goods prices.
paraphrases: Input costs kept rising faster than the prices firms charged for finished goods.
Nearly every District said input price growth outpaced growth in final goods prices.
Firms saw input costs climb quicker than what they could charge for final goods.
decoys: Nearly all reported that final goods prices rose faster than input costs.
Nearly all reported that input costs fell faster than final goods prices.

points.point: Overall price growth remained modest nationally, though a few Districts saw moderate increases
patterns: price\w*.{0,60}(modest pace|modest overall|remained modest|stayed modest)|(modest pace|modest overall|remained modest|stayed modest).{0,60}price\w*
points.quote: On balance, prices rose at a modest pace in most Districts, although a few noted moderate increases.
paraphrases: Prices rose at a modest pace overall in most Districts.
Overall price growth stayed modest, though a few Districts reported moderate increases.
Nationally, price increases remained modest on balance.
decoys: Prices surged nationally, accelerating sharply across most Districts.
Nearly all reported that input costs rose faster than final goods prices.

points.point: New home construction and existing home sales tended to decline or hold steady even as nonresidential construction and leasing tended to rise or remain flat.
points.quote: New home construction and existing home sales tended to decline or hold steady, while construction and leasing of nonresidential structures tended to rise or remain flat.
paraphrases: Residential construction and existing home sales were flat to down, while nonresidential construction and leasing rose or held flat.
Home sales and new construction softened or held steady, in contrast to gains in nonresidential construction and leasing.
While housing activity stalled or slipped, nonresidential construction and leasing activity improved or stayed flat.
decoys: New home construction and existing home sales tended to rise, while nonresidential construction declined.
New auto sales and used-car sales tended to decline or hold steady, while nonresidential construction rose.

points.point: About two-thirds of nonmanufacturing firms in the Third District anticipated increased activity over the next six months
points.quote: with two-thirds of the nonmanufacturing firms and over 40 percent of the manufacturers anticipating increases in general activity
paraphrases: About two-thirds of nonmanufacturing firms expected higher activity over the next six months.
Roughly 67% of nonmanufacturing contacts anticipated increased activity ahead.
Two-thirds of service-sector firms in the Third District foresaw growth in the next six months.
decoys: Just one-third of nonmanufacturing firms anticipated increases in general activity.
Over 40 percent of manufacturers anticipated increases in general activity.

points.point: Just over 40 percent of manufacturers in the Third District anticipated increased activity over the next six months
points.quote: with two-thirds of the nonmanufacturing firms and over 40 percent of the manufacturers anticipating increases in general activity
paraphrases: Just over 40% of manufacturers expected higher activity in the next six months.
About four in ten manufacturers anticipated increased general activity.
Over 40 percent of manufacturing contacts foresaw growth ahead.
decoys: About 20 percent of manufacturers anticipated increases in general activity.
Two-thirds of nonmanufacturing firms anticipated increases in general activity.

points.point: Soybeans normally exported to China were instead rerouted to other markets amid tariff-related trade tensions.
points.quote: Logistical challenges continued as soybeans that would usually be exported to China were being sent to other markets.
paraphrases: Soybeans typically bound for China were redirected to other buyers because of tariffs.
With China as a lost outlet, soybean exporters shipped to other markets instead.
Soybean shipments bound for China were instead diverted to alternative markets.
decoys: Soybean exports to China increased sharply as tariff tensions eased.
Corn shipments typically bound for China were redirected to other buyers because of tariffs.
